# CLAUDE.md

Guidance for Claude Code when working in `apps/commander-recommender/`.

## What this is

A Commander recommender: paste or upload a card list, get ranked Commander suggestions —
including Partner/Background pairs — with cited synergies, ban-list legality, and an estimated
Bracket. React 19 + Vite client (Zustand + TanStack Query/Table), Express 5 + better-sqlite3
server, no ORM. Card data is Scryfall's Oracle Cards bulk export, imported into SQLite at
build/deploy time — the running server never calls Scryfall live.

Read [`../../docs/commander-recommender.md`](../../docs/commander-recommender.md) first — it's
this app's own handoff document (moved here during the monorepo consolidation, file map kept
current) and covers the deeper "why" behind the stack choices, the scoring model, and known risk
areas in more depth than this file repeats. This file is about how to work in the code, not what
the code does. The root [`CLAUDE.md`](../../CLAUDE.md) covers workspace-wide commands and
conventions this file doesn't repeat.

## Commands

Run from `apps/commander-recommender/` unless noted (or use `pnpm --filter mtg-recommender-client`
/ `--filter mtg-recommender-server` from the repo root).

- `pnpm --filter mtg-recommender-client dev` and `pnpm --filter mtg-recommender-server dev`, or
  both via `pnpm dev` from the repo root — API on `:4000`, Vite client on `:5173` (proxies `/api`)
- `cd server && pnpm run prepare-data` — downloads Scryfall's Oracle Cards bulk file and seeds
  `server/data/cards.sqlite`; required before `/api/recommend` returns anything but a 503. Needs
  network access; reuses a copy less than a week old unless run as `prepare-data:fresh`
- `cd server && pnpm run typecheck` (`tsc`) / `pnpm run build` (`tsc -p tsconfig.build.json`,
  `src/` only, test files excluded — see the note in `tsconfig.build.json` about why `rootDir`
  matters here) / `pnpm test` (Vitest, 12 files colocated under `src/services/`)
- `cd client && pnpm run typecheck` (`tsc -b`) / `pnpm run build` (`tsc -b && vite build`) /
  `pnpm test` (Vitest, 5 files colocated under `src/lib/`)
- `pnpm run lint` in either — no type-aware rules (see `packages/config/eslint.base.js`)
- Single test file: `pnpm exec vitest run src/services/synergy.test.ts` (or any other), from
  whichever of `client`/`server` it lives in

## Architecture

- **`server/src/services/synergy.ts`** is the heart of the app: builds a `CollectionProfile` from
  the matched cards (color identity, creature types, keywords, oracle-text theme regexes), then
  scores every `CommanderUnit` from `partners.ts` against it. A signal counts only once it clears
  `MIN_SIGNAL_COUNT` (3) distinct supporting cards _after_ narrowing to that unit's color identity.
  Kindred requires the unit's own text to _care_ about a type (`caresAboutCreatureType`), not
  merely have it. Color identity gates eligibility and contributes nothing to score — see the
  "scoring measures focus" tests in `synergy.test.ts` before changing the weight formula.
- **`server/src/services/coverage.ts`** is a second, clearly-labelled tier beneath `synergy.ts`'s
  own two bars, not a lower bar on them — see
  [`../../docs/recommendation-coverage.md`](../../docs/recommendation-coverage.md). Every commander
  already in the submitted list gets suggested regardless of whether it clears `MIN_SIGNAL_COUNT`
  (reason `'owned'`), and a relaxed, narrowest-identity-first pick covers whatever card the
  confident tier still didn't cite (reason `'covers'`). `routes/recommend.ts` sends this as
  `alsoPlayable`, serialized through the same `serialize()`/`cardIndex` the confident `suggestions`
  use — never a second index.
- **`server/src/services/signals.ts`** (879 lines, the largest file) is the signal/role model
  feeding `synergy.ts`: what a card contributes to a deck's plan (`is`/`produces`/`consumes`/
  `rewards`/`amplifies`) and in what capacity. **Read
  [`../../docs/archetypes.md`](../../docs/archetypes.md) before changing this file** — it is the
  reviewable catalog of what those roles and archetypes are _meant_ to mean, derived from twenty real
  decks, and it records which current behaviours are deliberate (so they don't get "fixed") and which
  are known gaps. `deckAnalysis.ts` + `lifecycle.ts` + `packages.ts`
  build on it to answer "what is this list trying to do, and what's it missing" independent of any
  commander — see `docs/commander-recommender.md`'s file map for how those three fit together.
- **`server/src/services/partners.ts`** builds every legal `CommanderUnit` (rule 702.124: one card
  or a legal pair) from the eligible pool — a `CommanderUnit` is what `synergy.ts` scores, not a
  bare `CardRow`. Grouped by ability variant (Partner, Partner—[text], Partner with [Name], Friends
  forever, Choose a Background, Doctor's companion) rather than a cross-product.
- **`server/src/services/eligibility.ts`** judges commander eligibility on a card's **front face
  only** (CR 712.4) — Scryfall's top-level `type_line` for a DFC is both faces joined, which is why
  this can't just substring-match the whole thing. `split` is the deliberate exception (CR 709.4).
  This runs at import time (`import-scryfall.ts`'s only caller), so a stale `cards.sqlite` keeps
  old eligibility until re-imported.

  a stored `card_preferences` row (oracle_id only) back into a name/image, via `GET /api/cards`

  `services/cardDTO.ts` (`toCardDTO`), shared with `routes/recommend.ts` rather than duplicated.

  called from this app — see [`../../docs/api-policy.md`](../../docs/api-policy.md), a hard
  project rule, before changing what these call or when. The bulk-snapshot fetch/cache mechanics
  and `User-Agent` are shared with time-counters via `@mtg/scryfall` (`packages/scryfall`); this
  app's own companion fetches (creature types, re-skinned names) and its `IMPORT_VERSION`/sqlite

  and cites it by position; `client/src/lib/rehydrate.ts` puts cards back together at the API

  `refetchOnReconnect: false` defaults in `main.tsx` are load-bearing against Commander
  Spellbook traffic — don't restore them without re-reading the api-policy doc.

  virtualized (`@tanstack/react-virtual`), not paginated, so there's no "how many per page" to
  remember.

  combined platform static site (root `CLAUDE.md`'s "Combined deploy"), and `vite.config.ts`'s

  "Black/Green"). Mana glyph paths and cost parsing live in `@mtg/mana` (`packages/mana`), shared
  with the sibling app — this client has no `manaSymbols.ts` of its own anymore.

  this client's own `store/` — `useAuth`, `useCardPreferences`, `useComboPreferences`, all backed

## Conventions

- Comments explain _why_, not _what_ — match the existing tone (see `synergy.ts`'s comments on the
  scoring formula, or `eligibility.ts`'s on front-face-only reasoning).
- Keep changes proportional to the ask. This codebase deliberately favors a short, readable
  heuristic over a "complete" system in synergy detection and Bracket estimation — see
  `docs/commander-recommender.md`'s "Core logic" section before making one more sophisticated.
- Match the existing pattern for whichever file you're touching. If the surrounding code uses a
  plain function and a `Set`, don't reach for a class or a new dependency to do the same job.
- **Never write oracle text from memory — copy it from the database.** Scryfall has moved much
  self-referential wording from a card's name to "this creature"/"this land"; two rules in this
  codebase were written from recall and were wrong on real cards (see
  `docs/commander-recommender.md`'s "Known risk areas"). Every string in `signals.test.ts` is
  copied verbatim from the imported database — keep it that way.
- Before opening a PR: typecheck and test both `client/` and `server/`, and actually run the app
  for anything user-visible — a clean typecheck and passing tests are necessary, not sufficient
  (they don't catch a CSS rule that silently stopped applying, for instance).
- Add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry under `[Unreleased]` for any user-facing change, in the existing
  style (see `1.7.1`'s entry for the level of detail expected).
- `docs/commander-recommender.md`'s file map is meant to stay current — update it in the same
  commit whenever you add, rename, or remove a file it lists.

270:    * clause), or Evoke/Cleave/Delve/Convoke. Consumed by `freeSpells`. */
271:   alternativeCost: boolean;
272:   /** The card cares about a permanent being "modified" — CR's umbrella term
273:    * for having a counter on it, or an Equipment/Aura attached (Kodama of the
274:    * West Tree's own reminder text). Not itself a role yet — see
275:    * `alternativeCost`'s comment. */
276:   modified: boolean;
277:   /** The card's own text contains an actual "you win the game" outcome, not
278:    * a mere "can't lose/win" prevention effect (The Book of Exalted Deeds
279:    * grants the latter to an Angel, not the former, to itself). */
280:   alternateWin: boolean;
281: }

283: /**
284:  * Removes the card's own name from its oracle text.
285:  *
286:  * A card's rules text refers to itself by name, so any check that regexes a
287:  * word against oracle text will match that word for free when it appears in
288:  * the name. Goblin Sharpshooter's abilities are "doesn't untap", "whenever a
289:  * creature dies, untap" and a ping — it does not care about Goblins in the
290:  * slightest — yet it matched Goblin kindred purely because "Goblin" is in its
291:  * name. Names are not abilities, so they are removed before anything reads
292:  * the text.
293:  *
294:  * Both the full name and the pre-comma short form go, since rules text uses
295:  * the short form ("Lathril" for "Lathril, Blade of the Elves").
296:  */
297: export function stripSelfReferences(text: string, ...names: (string | null)[]): string {
298:   let out = text;
299:   const forms = new Set<string>();
300:   for (const name of names) {
301:     if (!name) continue;
302:     forms.add(name);
303:     // "Lathril, Blade of the Elves" -> also strip "Lathril".
304:     // .split() on any string always returns at least one element.
305:     const short = name.split(',')[0]!.trim();
306:     if (short && short !== name) forms.add(short);
307:   }
308:   // Longest first, so the full name goes before its own short form.
309:   for (const form of [...forms].sort((a, b) => b.length - a.length)) {
310:     out = out.split(form).join(' ');
311:   }
312:   return out;
313: }

315: /** Every word in a piece of text, lowercased. The unit of vocabulary
316:  * lookup — see `candidateTypes` for why looking up beats searching. */
317: function wordsIn(text: string): string[] {
318:   return text.toLowerCase().match(/[a-z][a-z'-]*/g) ?? [];
319: }

321: /**
322:  * Creature types of tokens this card creates.
323:  *
324:  * Read out of each "create ... token" clause, so a type mentioned elsewhere
325:  * in an unrelated sentence isn't credited as a token type.
326:  */
327: function findProducedTokenTypes(text: string, vocab: Vocabulary): string[] {
328:   const found = new Set<string>();
329:   for (const clause of text.match(/create[^.;]*token[^.;]*/gi) ?? []) {
330:     for (const word of wordsIn(clause)) {
331:       const type = vocab.typeByWord.get(word);
332:       if (type) found.add(type);
333:     }
334:   }
335:   return [...found];
336: }

338: /**
339:  * Creature types this card creates or grows via `amass` — "amass Orcs 1"
340:  * both grows (or creates) an Army token and turns it into the named type, so
341:  * it counts as producing both. The reminder explaining the mechanic is
342:  * stripped like any other, but the keyword's own printed name and type
343:  * argument survive.
344:  */
345: function findAmassedTypes(text: string, vocab: Vocabulary): string[] {
346:   const found = new Set<string>();
347:   for (const match of text.matchAll(/\bamass (\w+)/gi)) {
348:     found.add('Army');
349:     const type = vocab.typeByWord.get(match[1]!.toLowerCase());
350:     if (type) found.add(type);
351:   }
352:   return [...found];
353: }

355: /**
356:  * Lookup tables for the vocabulary signal detection recognises.
357:  *
358:  * Built once and reused across every card. The point is direction: with a
359:  * map, recognising a card's types costs one lookup per word it contains;
360:  * without one, it cost a regex per type in Magic. Across the card pool that
361:  * was the difference between ~8 seconds and ~82.
362:  */
363: export interface Vocabulary {
364:   /** Lowercased word, singular or plural, to its canonical creature type:
365:    * "elves" and "elf" both map to "Elf". */
366:   typeByWord: Map<string, string>;
367:   /** Lowercased single-word keyword to its canonical form. */
368:   keywordByWord: Map<string, string>;
369:   /** Keywords containing a space, which single-word lookup cannot find. */
370:   multiWordKeywords: string[];
371: }
372: 
373: export function buildVocabulary(creatureTypes: string[], keywords: string[]): Vocabulary {
374:   const typeByWord = new Map<string, string>();
375:   for (const type of creatureTypes) {
376:     typeByWord.set(type.toLowerCase(), type);
377:     typeByWord.set(pluralOfType(type).toLowerCase(), type);
378:   }
379: 
380:   const keywordByWord = new Map<string, string>();
381:   const multiWordKeywords: string[] = [];
382:   for (const keyword of keywords) {
383:     if (keyword.includes(' ')) multiWordKeywords.push(keyword);
384:     else keywordByWord.set(keyword.toLowerCase(), keyword);
385:   }
386: 
387:   return { typeByWord, keywordByWord, multiWordKeywords };
388: }

390: const wordPatternCache = new Map<string, RegExp>();
391: 
392: function escapeRegExp(value: string): string {
393:   return value.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');
394: }

396: /**
397:  * The English plural of a creature type, because cards refer to a type in the
398:  * aggregate — "Elves you control", not "Elf you control". Only the irregular
399:  * endings Magic's type list actually contains are handled.
400:  */
401: export function pluralOfType(type: string): string {
402:   // Elf -> Elves, Dwarf -> Dwarves. Lathril says "ten untapped Elves you
403:   // control", so missing this drops one of the format's best-known kindred
404:   // commanders.
405:   if (/f$/i.test(type)) return type.replace(/f$/i, 'ves');
406:   // Sphinx -> Sphinxes, Fungus -> Funguses, Leech -> Leeches.
407:   if (/(s|x|z|ch|sh)$/i.test(type)) return `${type}es`;
408:   return `${type}s`;
409: }

411: const tokenDescriptorCache = new Map<string, RegExp>();
412: 
413: /**
414:  * A token's printed type line inside a "create" clause — "Goblin creature
415:  * tokens", "Necron Warrior artifact creature tokens". Any number of
416:  * intervening words, since a token's full type line can carry several
417:  * subtypes and permanent types before "tokens" — one intervening word was
418:  * not enough to strip "Necron Warrior artifact creature tokens", and Their
419:  * Number Is Legion falsely read as a Necron payoff as a result.
420:  */
421: function tokenDescriptorPattern(type: string): RegExp {
422:   let pattern = tokenDescriptorCache.get(type);
423:   if (!pattern) {
424:     const forms = `(?:${escapeRegExp(type)}|${escapeRegExp(pluralOfType(type))})`;
425:     pattern = new RegExp(`\\b${forms}(?:\\s+\\w+)*\\s+(?:creature\\s+)?tokens?\\b`, 'gi');
426:     tokenDescriptorCache.set(type, pattern);
427:   }
428:   // Shared cached regex with /g — reset before each use.
429:   pattern.lastIndex = 0;
430:   return pattern;
431: }
432: 
433: /**
434:  * The card's own text with token-descriptor phrases ("Goblin creature
435:  * tokens") erased, but only *inside* a "create ... token" clause — the
436:  * Krenko's Command case the stripping exists for, mirroring
437:  * `findProducedTokenTypes`'s own clause-scoping. Stripping the same phrase
438:  * everywhere else is wrong: it erased Gleaming Overseer's "Zombie tokens you
439:  * control have hexproof and menace", Eternal Skylord's flying grant, and
440:  * Dreadhorde Invasion's attack trigger, none of which are inside a
441:  * token-creation clause.
442:  */
443: function withoutTokenDescriptors(text: string, type: string): string {
444:   return text.replace(/create[^.;]*token[^.;]*/gi, (clause) =>
445:     clause.replace(tokenDescriptorPattern(type), ' '),
446:   );
447: }

449: /** Matches a word or its plural, on a word boundary. Cached: this runs against
450:  * every candidate in a pool of thousands. */
451: function wordPattern(word: string): RegExp {
452:   let pattern = wordPatternCache.get(word);
453:   if (!pattern) {
454:     pattern = new RegExp(
455:       `\\b(?:${escapeRegExp(word)}|${escapeRegExp(pluralOfType(word))})\\b`,
456:       'i',
457:     );
458:     wordPatternCache.set(word, pattern);
459:   }
460:   return pattern;
461: }

463: /**
464:  * Whether the card sacrifices *itself*, as opposed to an indefinite object.
465:  *
466:  * Two spellings, because Scryfall changed theirs. Older text named the card
467:  * ("Sacrifice Arid Mesa:"); current text says "Sacrifice this land:" /
468:  * "Sacrifice this creature:". Both are read off the RAW text — the
469:  * name-stripped copy renders the first form as a bare "Sacrifice :".
470:  */
471: function detectsSelfSacrifice(rawText: string, names: string[]): boolean {
472:   if (/\bsacrifice this\b/i.test(rawText)) return true;
473:   return names.some((name) => {
474:     // .split() on any string always returns at least one element.
475:     const short = name.split(',')[0]!.trim();
476:     return short !== '' && new RegExp(`sacrifice ${escapeRegExp(short)}\\b`, 'i').test(rawText);
477:   });
478: }

480: /**
481:  * Whether every +1/+1 counter clause on the card targets only itself.
482:  *
483:  * Modeled on `detectsSelfSacrifice`: read off the RAW text, because
484:  * name-stripping destroys the evidence — "put a +1/+1 counter on Kalamax"
485:  * name-stripped is indistinguishable from a counter put on anything. A card
486:  * whose only counter clause grows itself (Kalamax's copy trigger,
487:  * Dragonsguard Elite's Magecraft) is not producing for a +1/+1 Counters
488:  * deck; a card with no counter clause at all trivially does not "grow only
489:  * itself" either.
490:  */
491: function detectsSelfGrowth(rawText: string, names: string[]): boolean {
492:   const counterClauses = clauses(rawText).filter((c) => /\+1\/\+1 counters?/i.test(c));
493:   if (counterClauses.length === 0) return false;
494:   const shortNames = names.map((name) => name.split(',')[0]!.trim()).filter((n) => n !== '');
495:   return counterClauses.every((clause) => {
496:     if (/\bon this (?:creature|permanent)\b/i.test(clause)) return true;
497:     return shortNames.some((short) => new RegExp(`\\bon ${escapeRegExp(short)}\\b`, 'i').test(clause));
498:   });
499: }

501: /** Quantifiers a sacrifice cost is phrased with, beyond the small set the
502:  * catalog used to test for — "one or more", "up to N", and "any number of"
503:  * all pay a real cost, and Plumb the Forbidden ("you may sacrifice one or
504:  * more creatures") matched none of the old set at all. */
505: const SACRIFICE_QUANTIFIER =
506:   'a|an|another|one or more|up to (?:one|two|three|four|five|six|seven|eight|nine|ten|\\d+)|' +
507:   'any number of|two|three|four|five|\\d+|x';
508: 
509: const sacrificeKindCache = new Map<string, RegExp>();
510: 
511: /** Everything before a clause's own `:`, or the whole clause if it has none
512:  * (a spell's additional cost, which is never an activated ability). */
513: function costSideOf(clause: string): string {
514:   const colon = clause.indexOf(':');
515:   return colon === -1 ? clause : clause.slice(0, colon);
516: }

518: /**
519:  * Whether a clause's COST sacrifices an object of the given kind — "a
520:  * creature", "a Zombie", "an artifact", "a token" — not merely mentions it
521:  * somewhere else in the same ability.
522:  *
523:  * Shared by `aristocrats.consumes` and `detectKindred`'s own consumes test,
524:  * which used to disagree about the same sentence in both directions:
525:  * Wilhelt's "you may sacrifice a Zombie" is a Zombie consumer but wasn't
526:  * recognised as a sacrifice outlet at all, because the old aristocrats
527:  * regex required the literal word "creature"; Sophia's "{1}, Sacrifice an
528:  * artifact token: Put a +1/+1 counter on each Dog you control" registered
529:  * as *consuming Dogs*, which she does not, because the old check read the
530:  * whole clause instead of just the cost.
531:  *
532:  * Deliberately excludes "sacrifices" (third person) — "Each player
533:  * sacrifices a creature" is an edict, not an outlet, and must keep failing.
534:  */
535: function sacrificesKind(clause: string, kind: string): boolean {
536:   let pattern = sacrificeKindCache.get(kind);
537:   if (!pattern) {
538:     const forms = `(?:${escapeRegExp(kind)}|${escapeRegExp(pluralOfType(kind))})`;
539:     pattern = new RegExp(`\\bsacrifice (?:${SACRIFICE_QUANTIFIER})\\b.*\\b${forms}\\b`, 'i');
540:     sacrificeKindCache.set(kind, pattern);
541:   }
542:   return pattern.test(costSideOf(clause));
543: }

545: const SACRIFICE_OBJECT_PATTERN = new RegExp(
546:   `\\bsacrifice (?:${SACRIFICE_QUANTIFIER})\\s+([a-z][a-z'-]*)`,
547:   'i',
548: );
549: 
550: /**
551:  * Whether a clause's cost sacrifices a creature — either the bare word
552:  * "creature[s]", or a named creature type the card never spells out
553:  * generically. Krenko's own sacrifice outlets (Goblin Bombardment,
554:  * Siege-Gang Commander, Arms Dealer, Goblin Grenade) all say "Sacrifice a
555:  * Goblin", never the word "creature".
556:  */
557: function sacrificesACreature(clause: string, vocab: Vocabulary): boolean {
558:   if (sacrificesKind(clause, 'creature')) return true;
559:   const match = SACRIFICE_OBJECT_PATTERN.exec(costSideOf(clause));
560:   return !!match && vocab.typeByWord.has(match[1]!.toLowerCase());
561: }

563: const TIME_COUNTER_PATTERN = new RegExp(`\\b(?:${TIME_COUNTER_KEYWORDS.join('|')})\\b`, 'i');
564: const MINUS_ONE_MINUS_ONE_PATTERN = new RegExp(
565:   `\\b(?:${MINUS_ONE_MINUS_ONE_KEYWORDS.map((k) => `${k}(?:s|ed|ing)?`).join('|')})\\b`,
566:   'i',
567: );
568: 
569: /**
570:  * Counter kinds named in the corpus beyond +1/+1 and -1/-1: stun (rule
571:  * 122.1d), lore (Sagas, rule 714), and the LOTR-set kinds — burden, oil,
572:  * corpse, supply, foreshadow, stash, eon, enlightened, loyalty. Each is
573:  * just a name from CR 122.1's glossary of counter types, recognised
574:  * generically ("<name> counter(s)") rather than as its own keyword ability.
575:  */
576: const NAMED_COUNTER_KINDS = [
577:   'stun',
578:   'lore',
579:   'burden',
580:   'oil',
581:   'corpse',
582:   'supply',
583:   'foreshadow',
584:   'stash',
585:   'eon',
586:   'enlightened',
587:   'loyalty',
588: ];

590: /**
591:  * The specific kind of counter a clause cares about — "+1/+1", "-1/-1",
592:  * "time" (Suspend/Vanishing/Time Travel), "stun", "loyalty", or whatever
593:  * named counter the card itself prints. Counters are a family, not a
594:  * keyword — the corpus alone needs at least a dozen kinds beyond the
595:  * literal string "+1/+1", and most of them (Blight, Persist, Suspend,
596:  * Vanishing) only ever name their counter inside reminder text that's
597:  * already stripped by the time this runs.
598:  *
599:  * Deliberately does NOT fall back to "whatever word precedes 'counter(s)'"
600:  * generically — The Ozolith's "if it had counters on it" would wrongly
601:  * extract "had" as a counter kind. A card that only ever says bare
602:  * "counters" stays unqualified on purpose.
603:  */
604: function findCounterKind(clause: string): string | undefined {
605:   const plusMinus = clause.match(/([+-]\d*\/[+-]\d*)\s+counters?/i);
606:   if (plusMinus) return plusMinus[1];
607:   if (MINUS_ONE_MINUS_ONE_PATTERN.test(clause)) return '-1/-1';
608:   if (TIME_COUNTER_PATTERN.test(clause) || /\btime counters?\b/i.test(clause)) return 'time';
609:   for (const kind of NAMED_COUNTER_KINDS) {
610:     if (new RegExp(`\\b${kind} counters?\\b`, 'i').test(clause)) return kind;
611:   }
612:   return undefined;
613: }

615: /** Every counter kind a card's own text cares about, for `supporterMatches`
616:  * (synergy.ts) to narrow a `counterType`-qualified signal's citable
617:  * supporters the same way it narrows `creatureType`/`keyword`. */
618: function findAllCounterKinds(text: string): string[] {
619:   const found = new Set<string>();
620:   for (const clause of clauses(text)) {
621:     const kind = findCounterKind(clause);
622:     if (kind) found.add(kind);
623:   }
624:   return [...found];
625: }

627: /** Keywords whose card is itself Max speed's or day/night's own mechanic,
628:  * rather than merely reading a state someone else produced — Momentum
629:  * Breaker's "Start your engines!", Graveyard Trespasser's "Daybound". */
630: const GAME_STATE_KEYWORDS: ReadonlyArray<readonly [string, string]> = [
631:   ['maxSpeed', 'Max speed'],
632:   ['maxSpeed', 'Start your engines!'],
633:   ['dayNight', 'Daybound'],
634:   ['dayNight', 'Nightbound'],
635: ];

637: /**
638:  * The persistent shared game state a clause produces or reads, if any — the
639:  * Ring, the monarch, the initiative, Max speed, and day/night. Unlike
640:  * `findCounterKind`'s vocabulary of counter kinds, these five have nothing
641:  * in common structurally, so each gets its own real-card-verified pattern
642:  * rather than one generic shape.
643:  *
644:  * Day/night is scoped to the actual templated phrases ("it's neither day
645:  * nor night", "it becomes day/night", "day becomes night") rather than the
646:  * bare words "day"/"night" — those appear in unrelated contexts too
647:  * (Replicating Ring's own "night counter", "Night Out in Vegas"'s mode
648:  * name), which the phrase-scoped pattern never matches.
649:  */
650: function findGameState(clause: string): string | undefined {
651:   if (/\bthe ring tempts you\b|\bring-bearer\b/i.test(clause)) return 'theRing';
652:   if (/\bthe monarch\b/i.test(clause)) return 'monarch';
653:   if (/\bthe initiative\b/i.test(clause)) return 'initiative';
654:   if (/\bmax speed\b|\byour engines\b/i.test(clause)) return 'maxSpeed';
655:   if (
656:     /\bit'?s (?:neither day nor night|day|night)\b|\bit becomes (?:day|night)\b|\bday becomes night\b|\bnight becomes day\b/i.test(
657:       clause,
658:     )
659:   ) {
660:     return 'dayNight';
661:   }
662:   return undefined;
663: }

665: /** Every game state a card's own keywords or text produce or read — see
666:  * `findGameState`. Feeds `qualifierKind: 'gameState'`. */
667: function findAllGameStates(text: string, keywords: string[]): string[] {
668:   const found = new Set<string>();
669:   for (const [state, keyword] of GAME_STATE_KEYWORDS) {
670:     if (keywords.includes(keyword)) found.add(state);
671:   }
672:   for (const clause of clauses(text)) {
673:     const state = findGameState(clause);
674:     if (state) found.add(state);
675:   }
676:   return [...found];
677: }

679: /**
680:  * Whether a clause makes `subject` cheaper or free — "Equipment spells you
681:  * cast cost {1} less", "equip {0}", "pay {0} rather than pay the equip
682:  * cost", "the second spell you cast each turn costs {2} less". Modelled once
683:  * and parameterised by what it reduces, rather than a bespoke regex per
684:  * archetype: Danitha (Aura and Equipment spells), Puresteel Paladin (equip
685:  * {0}), Bruenor Battlehammer (free equip), Bladehold War-Whip (other
686:  * Equipment's own equip cost), and Alisaie Leveilleur's Dualcast (the second
687:  * spell each turn) are all this same shape. Cost reduction is `enables`, not
688:  * `rewards` — it turns the engine on faster, it doesn't reward you for
689:  * having engaged with it.
690:  */
691: function reducesCostOf(text: string, subject: RegExp): boolean {
692:   return clauses(text).some(
693:     (clause) => subject.test(clause) && /costs? \{?\d|pay \{0\}|equip \{0\}/i.test(clause),
694:   );
695: }

697: /**
698:  * The individual face names inside a Scryfall-joined card name
699:  * ("Front // Back" -> ["Front", "Back"]). A single-faced card's name has no
700:  * " // " and splits into just itself.
701:  *
702:  * Needed because oracle text names only the face it belongs to ("Stomp
703:  * deals 2 damage...", never "Bonecrusher Giant // Stomp deals..."), but
704:  * `row.back_name` alone doesn't cover this — it's null for split, adventure,
705:  * and flip layouts (see @mtg/card-model's isTwoSidedLayout, which reserves
706:  * it for transform/modal_dfc only), even though those layouts join their
707:  * stored `name` with " // " the exact same way. Without this, a bare face
708:  * name in oracle text (Bonecrusher Giant's Adventure half, "Stomp") was
709:  * never recognised as a self-reference and so never stripped.
710:  */
711: function faceNamesIn(name: string): string[] {
712:   return name.split(' // ');
713: }

715: /**
716:  * Removes reminder text — the parenthetical restatement of a keyword.
717:  *
718:  * Reminder text explains a keyword the card already has; it is never an
719:  * ability of its own. Leaving it in produced real false positives: Sliver
720:  * Gravemother's Encore reminder text ends "They gain haste", which read as
721:  * the card *granting* haste to your team, i.e. an active Haste payoff.
722:  */
723: function stripReminderText(text: string): string {
724:   return text.replace(/\([^)]*\)/g, ' ');
725: }

727: /**
728:  * Normalises two "lord" templating variants onto the one shape the rest of
729:  * the catalog expects — "<Type> creatures you control get/gain/have" —
730:  * rather than adding a third regex for each archetype that cares.
731:  *
732:  * Older wording omits "you control" ("All Sliver creatures get +1/+1", Muscle
733:  * Sliver); other cards omit "creatures" ("Zombies you control get +1/+1",
734:  * Tomb Tyrant). Functionally identical lords, sorted by which decade the card
735:  * was printed in. Scoped to known creature-type words specifically, so it
736:  * can't misfire on "for each land you control" or similar unrelated phrasing.
737:  */
738: function normalizeLordWording(text: string, vocab: Vocabulary): string {
739:   let out = text.replace(/\ball ([a-z][a-z'-]*) creatures\b/gi, (whole, word: string) =>
740:     vocab.typeByWord.has(word.toLowerCase()) ? `${word} creatures you control` : whole,
741:   );
742:   out = out.replace(
743:     /\b([a-z][a-z'-]*) you control (get|gain|have|gets|gains)\b/gi,
744:     (whole, word: string, verb: string) =>
745:       vocab.typeByWord.has(word.toLowerCase()) ? `${word} creatures you control ${verb}` : whole,
746:   );
747:   return out;
748: }

750: /** The card types a `cardType` qualifier can narrow to — the part of the
751:  * type line before the em dash, supertypes (Legendary, Basic, Snow, World,
752:  * Ongoing) excluded because they say nothing about what the card *is*. */
753: const CARD_TYPES = [
754:   'Creature',
755:   'Instant',
756:   'Sorcery',
757:   'Artifact',
758:   'Enchantment',
759:   'Land',
760:   'Planeswalker',
761:   'Battle',
762:   'Kindred',
763: ];
764: 
765: function findCardTypes(typeLine: string): string[] {
766:   const beforeDash = typeLine.split('—')[0] ?? typeLine;

4:  *
5:  * This replaces the old flat "theme" model, in which a signal was a single
6:  * regex applied identically to your card and to the candidate commander, and
7:  * two cards "synergised" when the same words appeared in both. That measured
8:  * lexical co-occurrence rather than synergy: "Sacrifice a creature" and
9:  * "Sacrifice Arid Mesa" are the same word and completely different mechanics,
10:  * and a commander that pays off a plan (Craterhoof Behemoth pumping your
11:  * board) usually shares no vocabulary at all with the cards that set it up.
12:  *
13:  * Three ideas do the work here.
14:  *
15:  * 1. ROLES. A card doesn't just "have" a theme, it participates in one in a
16:  *    particular capacity — see `Role`. This is what lets one card carry
17:  *    several unrelated signals: Goblin Sharpshooter is Goblin kindred because
18:  *    of its creature *type*, and part of the creature-death cluster because of
19:  *    its *text*, and those two facts have nothing to do with each other.
20:  *
21:  * 2. TWO SIDES. Membership in a group is read off structured data wherever it
22:  *    exists (creature types, keywords, type line); qualifying as a *payoff*
23:  *    is read off rules text. A card's NAME is never evidence of anything —
24:  *    see `stripSelfReferences` for why that mattered.
25:  *
26:  * 3. QUALIFIERS. A payoff can be restricted to a subtype, and then it only
27:  *    pays off cards of that subtype. Sliver Gravemother cares about Slivers
28:  *    in the graveyard, so it feeds "Reanimator (Sliver)" — not generic
29:  *    Reanimator — and every non-Sliver creature in your bin is worth nothing
30:  *    to it.
31:  *
32:  * Extending this: adding an archetype means adding one entry to `ARCHETYPES`
33:  * with per-role matchers. `Role`, `QualifierKind` and the catalog are all
34:  * meant to grow; nothing here is closed.
35:  */
36: import { MINUS_ONE_MINUS_ONE_KEYWORDS, TIME_COUNTER_KEYWORDS } from '@mtg/rules';
37: import { parseJsonArray, type CardRow } from '../types';

39: /**
40:  * The capacity in which a card participates in an archetype.
41:  *
42:  * This vocabulary replaced an earlier "Outlet / Payoff" split that was
43:  * reported as "not quite right" — the two are almost never separable on a
44:  * real card: Lathril's activated ability *consumes* ten Elves and *rewards*
45:  * you in the same breath, and Viscera Seer is a sacrifice outlet whose whole
46:  * point is the scry it gives back. Splitting "consumes" from "rewards" lets
47:  * one ability be both, which Outlet/Payoff could not express.
48:  *
49:  * `enables` and `protects` were added once three decks made a real gap
50:  * expensive to leave unnamed: Obeka's whole deck is three cards that erase a
51:  * delayed sacrifice trigger 25 other cards carry; Kalamax runs six cards that
52:  * tap a creature for mana purely to turn him on at instant speed; and Bre's
53:  * Puresteel Paladin/Bruenor/Danitha (equip-cost reduction, free equip) read
54:  * as payoffs in every practical sense but fail every `rewards` matcher, and
55:  * correctly so — they don't reward you for anything, they make the engine
56:  * easier to run. Goblin Sharpshooter (`rewards` on creature-death here, since
57:  * it untaps when a creature dies) is the same shape read backwards: it's
58:  * often *described* as a sacrifice outlet, because it becomes a machine gun
59:  * with any real outlet, but it enables a loop it does not itself contain.
60:  *
61:  * `is` on a vanilla creature is deliberately not wired into Aristocrats, even
62:  * though a vanilla creature genuinely is sacrifice fodder — counting it
63:  * would make every creature deck read as Aristocrats.
64:  */
65: export type Role =
66:   /** The card *is* the resource: a Goblin, an Equipment, a land. Structured
67:    * data, never text. Passive — see `ACTIVE_ROLES`. */
68:   | 'is'
69:   /** The card *makes* the resource: Goblin tokens, extra land drops, cards
70:    * into your own graveyard. */
71:   | 'produces'
72:   /** The card *needs* the resource, as a cost or a requirement: "Sacrifice a
73:    * creature:", "Tap ten untapped Elves:". */
74:   | 'consumes'
75:   /** The card *benefits* from the resource existing or the event happening:
76:    * Blood Artist, Craterhoof Behemoth, Teysa buffing your tokens. */
77:   | 'rewards'
78:   /** The card *doubles or repeats* the resource or event: Doubling Season,
79:    * Teysa making death triggers fire twice. A card that only amplifies needs
80:    * something else to amplify — it generates no value alone. */
81:   | 'amplifies'
82:   /** The card *turns the engine on* without being it: cost reduction, free
83:    * casts/activations, erasing a delayed trigger. Obeka is a whole deck whose
84:    * thesis is three enablers; Puresteel Paladin's `equip {0}` is a Voltron
85:    * payoff in every practical sense but rewards nothing. */
86:   | 'enables'
87:   /** The card *keeps the engine running*. Must be archetype-scoped — Sliver
88:    * Hivelord protects Slivers specifically ("Sliver creatures you control
89:    * have indestructible"), never generic hexproof/protection, or every
90:    * Lightning Greaves becomes a candidate for everything. */
91:   | 'protects';
92: 
93: export const ROLES: Role[] = [
94:   'is',
95:   'produces',
96:   'consumes',
97:   'rewards',
98:   'amplifies',
99:   'enables',
100:   'protects',
101: ];

103: /**
104:  * Roles that mean the card actually engages with the plan, as opposed to
105:  * merely being a member of a group.
106:  *
107:  * This is the generalisation of the old "cares, not shares" kindred rule: a
108:  * commander needs at least one active role to be suggested for an archetype.
109:  * Silas Renn *is* a Human (`is`) and never mentions Humans, so he is not a
110:  * Human commander. Krenko *produces* Goblins and *rewards* having them, so he
111:  * is. The same test now covers keywords for free — having Trample is `is`,
112:  * granting it to your team is `produces`.
113:  */
114: export const ACTIVE_ROLES: Role[] = [
115:   'produces',
116:   'consumes',
117:   'rewards',
118:   'amplifies',
119:   'enables',
120:   'protects',
121: ];

123: export function hasActiveRole(roles: Role[]): boolean {
124:   return roles.some((r) => ACTIVE_ROLES.includes(r));

283: /**
284:  * Removes the card's own name from its oracle text.
285:  *
286:  * A card's rules text refers to itself by name, so any check that regexes a
287:  * word against oracle text will match that word for free when it appears in
288:  * the name. Goblin Sharpshooter's abilities are "doesn't untap", "whenever a
289:  * creature dies, untap" and a ping — it does not care about Goblins in the
290:  * slightest — yet it matched Goblin kindred purely because "Goblin" is in its
291:  * name. Names are not abilities, so they are removed before anything reads
292:  * the text.
293:  *
294:  * Both the full name and the pre-comma short form go, since rules text uses
295:  * the short form ("Lathril" for "Lathril, Blade of the Elves").
296:  */
297: export function stripSelfReferences(text: string, ...names: (string | null)[]): string {
298:   let out = text;
299:   const forms = new Set<string>();
300:   for (const name of names) {
301:     if (!name) continue;
302:     forms.add(name);
303:     // "Lathril, Blade of the Elves" -> also strip "Lathril".
304:     // .split() on any string always returns at least one element.
305:     const short = name.split(',')[0]!.trim();
306:     if (short && short !== name) forms.add(short);
307:   }
308:   // Longest first, so the full name goes before its own short form.
309:   for (const form of [...forms].sort((a, b) => b.length - a.length)) {
310:     out = out.split(form).join(' ');
311:   }
312:   return out;
313: }

315: /** Every word in a piece of text, lowercased. The unit of vocabulary
316:  * lookup — see `candidateTypes` for why looking up beats searching. */
317: function wordsIn(text: string): string[] {
318:   return text.toLowerCase().match(/[a-z][a-z'-]*/g) ?? [];
319: }

321: /**
322:  * Creature types of tokens this card creates.
323:  *
324:  * Read out of each "create ... token" clause, so a type mentioned elsewhere
325:  * in an unrelated sentence isn't credited as a token type.
326:  */
327: function findProducedTokenTypes(text: string, vocab: Vocabulary): string[] {
328:   const found = new Set<string>();
329:   for (const clause of text.match(/create[^.;]*token[^.;]*/gi) ?? []) {
330:     for (const word of wordsIn(clause)) {
331:       const type = vocab.typeByWord.get(word);
332:       if (type) found.add(type);
333:     }
334:   }
335:   return [...found];
336: }

338: /**
339:  * Creature types this card creates or grows via `amass` — "amass Orcs 1"
340:  * both grows (or creates) an Army token and turns it into the named type, so
341:  * it counts as producing both. The reminder explaining the mechanic is
342:  * stripped like any other, but the keyword's own printed name and type
343:  * argument survive.
344:  */
345: function findAmassedTypes(text: string, vocab: Vocabulary): string[] {
346:   const found = new Set<string>();
347:   for (const match of text.matchAll(/\bamass (\w+)/gi)) {
348:     found.add('Army');
349:     const type = vocab.typeByWord.get(match[1]!.toLowerCase());
350:     if (type) found.add(type);
351:   }
352:   return [...found];
353: }

355: /**
356:  * Lookup tables for the vocabulary signal detection recognises.
357:  *
358:  * Built once and reused across every card. The point is direction: with a
359:  * map, recognising a card's types costs one lookup per word it contains;
360:  * without one, it cost a regex per type in Magic. Across the card pool that
361:  * was the difference between ~8 seconds and ~82.
362:  */
363: export interface Vocabulary {
364:   /** Lowercased word, singular or plural, to its canonical creature type:
365:    * "elves" and "elf" both map to "Elf". */
366:   typeByWord: Map<string, string>;
367:   /** Lowercased single-word keyword to its canonical form. */
368:   keywordByWord: Map<string, string>;
369:   /** Keywords containing a space, which single-word lookup cannot find. */
370:   multiWordKeywords: string[];
371: }

373: export function buildVocabulary(creatureTypes: string[], keywords: string[]): Vocabulary {
374:   const typeByWord = new Map<string, string>();
375:   for (const type of creatureTypes) {
376:     typeByWord.set(type.toLowerCase(), type);
377:     typeByWord.set(pluralOfType(type).toLowerCase(), type);
378:   }
379: 
380:   const keywordByWord = new Map<string, string>();
381:   const multiWordKeywords: string[] = [];
382:   for (const keyword of keywords) {
383:     if (keyword.includes(' ')) multiWordKeywords.push(keyword);
384:     else keywordByWord.set(keyword.toLowerCase(), keyword);
385:   }
386: 
387:   return { typeByWord, keywordByWord, multiWordKeywords };
388: }

390: const wordPatternCache = new Map<string, RegExp>();

392: function escapeRegExp(value: string): string {
393:   return value.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');
394: }

396: /**
397:  * The English plural of a creature type, because cards refer to a type in the
398:  * aggregate — "Elves you control", not "Elf you control". Only the irregular
399:  * endings Magic's type list actually contains are handled.
400:  */
401: export function pluralOfType(type: string): string {
402:   // Elf -> Elves, Dwarf -> Dwarves. Lathril says "ten untapped Elves you
403:   // control", so missing this drops one of the format's best-known kindred
404:   // commanders.
405:   if (/f$/i.test(type)) return type.replace(/f$/i, 'ves');
406:   // Sphinx -> Sphinxes, Fungus -> Funguses, Leech -> Leeches.
407:   if (/(s|x|z|ch|sh)$/i.test(type)) return `${type}es`;
408:   return `${type}s`;
409: }

411: const tokenDescriptorCache = new Map<string, RegExp>();

413: /**
414:  * A token's printed type line inside a "create" clause — "Goblin creature
415:  * tokens", "Necron Warrior artifact creature tokens". Any number of
416:  * intervening words, since a token's full type line can carry several
417:  * subtypes and permanent types before "tokens" — one intervening word was
418:  * not enough to strip "Necron Warrior artifact creature tokens", and Their
419:  * Number Is Legion falsely read as a Necron payoff as a result.
420:  */
421: function tokenDescriptorPattern(type: string): RegExp {
422:   let pattern = tokenDescriptorCache.get(type);
423:   if (!pattern) {
424:     const forms = `(?:${escapeRegExp(type)}|${escapeRegExp(pluralOfType(type))})`;
425:     pattern = new RegExp(`\\b${forms}(?:\\s+\\w+)*\\s+(?:creature\\s+)?tokens?\\b`, 'gi');
426:     tokenDescriptorCache.set(type, pattern);
427:   }
428:   // Shared cached regex with /g — reset before each use.
429:   pattern.lastIndex = 0;
430:   return pattern;
431: }

433: /**
434:  * The card's own text with token-descriptor phrases ("Goblin creature
435:  * tokens") erased, but only *inside* a "create ... token" clause — the
436:  * Krenko's Command case the stripping exists for, mirroring
437:  * `findProducedTokenTypes`'s own clause-scoping. Stripping the same phrase
438:  * everywhere else is wrong: it erased Gleaming Overseer's "Zombie tokens you
439:  * control have hexproof and menace", Eternal Skylord's flying grant, and
440:  * Dreadhorde Invasion's attack trigger, none of which are inside a
441:  * token-creation clause.
442:  */
443: function withoutTokenDescriptors(text: string, type: string): string {
444:   return text.replace(/create[^.;]*token[^.;]*/gi, (clause) =>
445:     clause.replace(tokenDescriptorPattern(type), ' '),
446:   );
447: }

449: /** Matches a word or its plural, on a word boundary. Cached: this runs against
450:  * every candidate in a pool of thousands. */
451: function wordPattern(word: string): RegExp {
452:   let pattern = wordPatternCache.get(word);
453:   if (!pattern) {
454:     pattern = new RegExp(
455:       `\\b(?:${escapeRegExp(word)}|${escapeRegExp(pluralOfType(word))})\\b`,
456:       'i',
457:     );
458:     wordPatternCache.set(word, pattern);
459:   }
460:   return pattern;
461: }

463: /**
464:  * Whether the card sacrifices *itself*, as opposed to an indefinite object.
465:  *
466:  * Two spellings, because Scryfall changed theirs. Older text named the card
467:  * ("Sacrifice Arid Mesa:"); current text says "Sacrifice this land:" /
468:  * "Sacrifice this creature:". Both are read off the RAW text — the
469:  * name-stripped copy renders the first form as a bare "Sacrifice :".
470:  */
471: function detectsSelfSacrifice(rawText: string, names: string[]): boolean {
472:   if (/\bsacrifice this\b/i.test(rawText)) return true;
473:   return names.some((name) => {
474:     // .split() on any string always returns at least one element.
475:     const short = name.split(',')[0]!.trim();
476:     return short !== '' && new RegExp(`sacrifice ${escapeRegExp(short)}\\b`, 'i').test(rawText);
477:   });
478: }

480: /**
481:  * Whether every +1/+1 counter clause on the card targets only itself.
482:  *
483:  * Modeled on `detectsSelfSacrifice`: read off the RAW text, because
484:  * name-stripping destroys the evidence — "put a +1/+1 counter on Kalamax"
485:  * name-stripped is indistinguishable from a counter put on anything. A card
486:  * whose only counter clause grows itself (Kalamax's copy trigger,
487:  * Dragonsguard Elite's Magecraft) is not producing for a +1/+1 Counters
488:  * deck; a card with no counter clause at all trivially does not "grow only
489:  * itself" either.
490:  */
491: function detectsSelfGrowth(rawText: string, names: string[]): boolean {
492:   const counterClauses = clauses(rawText).filter((c) => /\+1\/\+1 counters?/i.test(c));
493:   if (counterClauses.length === 0) return false;
494:   const shortNames = names.map((name) => name.split(',')[0]!.trim()).filter((n) => n !== '');
495:   return counterClauses.every((clause) => {
496:     if (/\bon this (?:creature|permanent)\b/i.test(clause)) return true;
497:     return shortNames.some((short) => new RegExp(`\\bon ${escapeRegExp(short)}\\b`, 'i').test(clause));
498:   });
499: }

501: /** Quantifiers a sacrifice cost is phrased with, beyond the small set the
502:  * catalog used to test for — "one or more", "up to N", and "any number of"
503:  * all pay a real cost, and Plumb the Forbidden ("you may sacrifice one or
504:  * more creatures") matched none of the old set at all. */
505: const SACRIFICE_QUANTIFIER =
506:   'a|an|another|one or more|up to (?:one|two|three|four|five|six|seven|eight|nine|ten|\\d+)|' +
507:   'any number of|two|three|four|five|\\d+|x';

509: const sacrificeKindCache = new Map<string, RegExp>();

511: /** Everything before a clause's own `:`, or the whole clause if it has none
512:  * (a spell's additional cost, which is never an activated ability). */
513: function costSideOf(clause: string): string {
514:   const colon = clause.indexOf(':');
515:   return colon === -1 ? clause : clause.slice(0, colon);
516: }

518: /**
519:  * Whether a clause's COST sacrifices an object of the given kind — "a
520:  * creature", "a Zombie", "an artifact", "a token" — not merely mentions it
521:  * somewhere else in the same ability.
522:  *
523:  * Shared by `aristocrats.consumes` and `detectKindred`'s own consumes test,
524:  * which used to disagree about the same sentence in both directions:
525:  * Wilhelt's "you may sacrifice a Zombie" is a Zombie consumer but wasn't
526:  * recognised as a sacrifice outlet at all, because the old aristocrats
527:  * regex required the literal word "creature"; Sophia's "{1}, Sacrifice an
528:  * artifact token: Put a +1/+1 counter on each Dog you control" registered
529:  * as *consuming Dogs*, which she does not, because the old check read the
530:  * whole clause instead of just the cost.
531:  *
532:  * Deliberately excludes "sacrifices" (third person) — "Each player
533:  * sacrifices a creature" is an edict, not an outlet, and must keep failing.
534:  */
535: function sacrificesKind(clause: string, kind: string): boolean {
536:   let pattern = sacrificeKindCache.get(kind);
537:   if (!pattern) {
538:     const forms = `(?:${escapeRegExp(kind)}|${escapeRegExp(pluralOfType(kind))})`;
539:     pattern = new RegExp(`\\bsacrifice (?:${SACRIFICE_QUANTIFIER})\\b.*\\b${forms}\\b`, 'i');
540:     sacrificeKindCache.set(kind, pattern);
541:   }
542:   return pattern.test(costSideOf(clause));
543: }

545: const SACRIFICE_OBJECT_PATTERN = new RegExp(
546:   `\\bsacrifice (?:${SACRIFICE_QUANTIFIER})\\s+([a-z][a-z'-]*)`,
547:   'i',
548: );

550: /**
551:  * Whether a clause's cost sacrifices a creature — either the bare word
552:  * "creature[s]", or a named creature type the card never spells out
553:  * generically. Krenko's own sacrifice outlets (Goblin Bombardment,
554:  * Siege-Gang Commander, Arms Dealer, Goblin Grenade) all say "Sacrifice a
555:  * Goblin", never the word "creature".
556:  */
557: function sacrificesACreature(clause: string, vocab: Vocabulary): boolean {
558:   if (sacrificesKind(clause, 'creature')) return true;
559:   const match = SACRIFICE_OBJECT_PATTERN.exec(costSideOf(clause));
560:   return !!match && vocab.typeByWord.has(match[1]!.toLowerCase());
561: }

563: const TIME_COUNTER_PATTERN = new RegExp(`\\b(?:${TIME_COUNTER_KEYWORDS.join('|')})\\b`, 'i');
564: const MINUS_ONE_MINUS_ONE_PATTERN = new RegExp(
565:   `\\b(?:${MINUS_ONE_MINUS_ONE_KEYWORDS.map((k) => `${k}(?:s|ed|ing)?`).join('|')})\\b`,
566:   'i',
567: );

569: /**
570:  * Counter kinds named in the corpus beyond +1/+1 and -1/-1: stun (rule
571:  * 122.1d), lore (Sagas, rule 714), and the LOTR-set kinds — burden, oil,
572:  * corpse, supply, foreshadow, stash, eon, enlightened, loyalty. Each is
573:  * just a name from CR 122.1's glossary of counter types, recognised
574:  * generically ("<name> counter(s)") rather than as its own keyword ability.
575:  */
576: const NAMED_COUNTER_KINDS = [
577:   'stun',
578:   'lore',
579:   'burden',
580:   'oil',
581:   'corpse',
582:   'supply',
583:   'foreshadow',
584:   'stash',
585:   'eon',
586:   'enlightened',
587:   'loyalty',
588: ];

590: /**
591:  * The specific kind of counter a clause cares about — "+1/+1", "-1/-1",
592:  * "time" (Suspend/Vanishing/Time Travel), "stun", "loyalty", or whatever
593:  * named counter the card itself prints. Counters are a family, not a
594:  * keyword — the corpus alone needs at least a dozen kinds beyond the
595:  * literal string "+1/+1", and most of them (Blight, Persist, Suspend,
596:  * Vanishing) only ever name their counter inside reminder text that's
597:  * already stripped by the time this runs.
598:  *
599:  * Deliberately does NOT fall back to "whatever word precedes 'counter(s)'"
600:  * generically — The Ozolith's "if it had counters on it" would wrongly
601:  * extract "had" as a counter kind. A card that only ever says bare
602:  * "counters" stays unqualified on purpose.
603:  */
604: function findCounterKind(clause: string): string | undefined {
605:   const plusMinus = clause.match(/([+-]\d*\/[+-]\d*)\s+counters?/i);
606:   if (plusMinus) return plusMinus[1];
607:   if (MINUS_ONE_MINUS_ONE_PATTERN.test(clause)) return '-1/-1';
608:   if (TIME_COUNTER_PATTERN.test(clause) || /\btime counters?\b/i.test(clause)) return 'time';
609:   for (const kind of NAMED_COUNTER_KINDS) {
610:     if (new RegExp(`\\b${kind} counters?\\b`, 'i').test(clause)) return kind;
611:   }
612:   return undefined;
613: }

615: /** Every counter kind a card's own text cares about, for `supporterMatches`
616:  * (synergy.ts) to narrow a `counterType`-qualified signal's citable
617:  * supporters the same way it narrows `creatureType`/`keyword`. */
618: function findAllCounterKinds(text: string): string[] {
619:   const found = new Set<string>();
620:   for (const clause of clauses(text)) {
621:     const kind = findCounterKind(clause);
622:     if (kind) found.add(kind);
623:   }
624:   return [...found];
625: }

627: /** Keywords whose card is itself Max speed's or day/night's own mechanic,
628:  * rather than merely reading a state someone else produced — Momentum
629:  * Breaker's "Start your engines!", Graveyard Trespasser's "Daybound". */
630: const GAME_STATE_KEYWORDS: ReadonlyArray<readonly [string, string]> = [
631:   ['maxSpeed', 'Max speed'],
632:   ['maxSpeed', 'Start your engines!'],
633:   ['dayNight', 'Daybound'],
634:   ['dayNight', 'Nightbound'],
635: ];

637: /**
638:  * The persistent shared game state a clause produces or reads, if any — the
639:  * Ring, the monarch, the initiative, Max speed, and day/night. Unlike
640:  * `findCounterKind`'s vocabulary of counter kinds, these five have nothing
641:  * in common structurally, so each gets its own real-card-verified pattern
642:  * rather than one generic shape.
643:  *
644:  * Day/night is scoped to the actual templated phrases ("it's neither day
645:  * nor night", "it becomes day/night", "day becomes night") rather than the
646:  * bare words "day"/"night" — those appear in unrelated contexts too
647:  * (Replicating Ring's own "night counter", "Night Out in Vegas"'s mode
648:  * name), which the phrase-scoped pattern never matches.
649:  */
650: function findGameState(clause: string): string | undefined {
651:   if (/\bthe ring tempts you\b|\bring-bearer\b/i.test(clause)) return 'theRing';
652:   if (/\bthe monarch\b/i.test(clause)) return 'monarch';
653:   if (/\bthe initiative\b/i.test(clause)) return 'initiative';
654:   if (/\bmax speed\b|\byour engines\b/i.test(clause)) return 'maxSpeed';
655:   if (
656:     /\bit'?s (?:neither day nor night|day|night)\b|\bit becomes (?:day|night)\b|\bday becomes night\b|\bnight becomes day\b/i.test(
657:       clause,
658:     )
659:   ) {
660:     return 'dayNight';
661:   }
662:   return undefined;
663: }

665: /** Every game state a card's own keywords or text produce or read — see
666:  * `findGameState`. Feeds `qualifierKind: 'gameState'`. */
667: function findAllGameStates(text: string, keywords: string[]): string[] {
668:   const found = new Set<string>();
669:   for (const [state, keyword] of GAME_STATE_KEYWORDS) {
670:     if (keywords.includes(keyword)) found.add(state);
671:   }
672:   for (const clause of clauses(text)) {
673:     const state = findGameState(clause);
674:     if (state) found.add(state);
675:   }
676:   return [...found];
677: }

679: /**
680:  * Whether a clause makes `subject` cheaper or free — "Equipment spells you
681:  * cast cost {1} less", "equip {0}", "pay {0} rather than pay the equip
682:  * cost", "the second spell you cast each turn costs {2} less". Modelled once
683:  * and parameterised by what it reduces, rather than a bespoke regex per
684:  * archetype: Danitha (Aura and Equipment spells), Puresteel Paladin (equip
685:  * {0}), Bruenor Battlehammer (free equip), Bladehold War-Whip (other
686:  * Equipment's own equip cost), and Alisaie Leveilleur's Dualcast (the second
687:  * spell each turn) are all this same shape. Cost reduction is `enables`, not
688:  * `rewards` — it turns the engine on faster, it doesn't reward you for
689:  * having engaged with it.

691: function reducesCostOf(text: string, subject: RegExp): boolean {
692:   return clauses(text).some(
693:     (clause) => subject.test(clause) && /costs? \{?\d|pay \{0\}|equip \{0\}/i.test(clause),

697: /**
698:  * The individual face names inside a Scryfall-joined card name
699:  * ("Front // Back" -> ["Front", "Back"]). A single-faced card's name has no
700:  * " // " and splits into just itself.

702:  * Needed because oracle text names only the face it belongs to ("Stomp
703:  * deals 2 damage...", never "Bonecrusher Giant // Stomp deals..."), but
704:  * `row.back_name` alone doesn't cover this — it's null for split, adventure,
705:  * and flip layouts (see @mtg/card-model's isTwoSidedLayout, which reserves
706:  * it for transform/modal_dfc only), even though those layouts join their
707:  * stored `name` with " // " the exact same way. Without this, a bare face
708:  * name in oracle text (Bonecrusher Giant's Adventure half, "Stomp") was
709:  * never recognised as a self-reference and so never stripped.
710:  */
711: function faceNamesIn(name: string): string[] {
712:   return name.split(' // ');
713: }

715: /**
716:  * Removes reminder text — the parenthetical restatement of a keyword.
717:  *
718:  * Reminder text explains a keyword the card already has; it is never an
719:  * ability of its own. Leaving it in produced real false positives: Sliver
720:  * Gravemother's Encore reminder text ends "They gain haste", which read as
721:  * the card *granting* haste to your team, i.e. an active Haste payoff.
722:  */

724:   return text.replace(/\([^)]*\)/g, ' ');

727: /**
728:  * Normalises two "lord" templating variants onto the one shape the rest of
729:  * the catalog expects — "<Type> creatures you control get/gain/have" —
730:  * rather than adding a third regex for each archetype that cares.
731:  *
732:  * Older wording omits "you control" ("All Sliver creatures get +1/+1", Muscle
733:  * Sliver); other cards omit "creatures" ("Zombies you control get +1/+1",
734:  * Tomb Tyrant). Functionally identical lords, sorted by which decade the card
735:  * was printed in. Scoped to known creature-type words specifically, so it
736:  * can't misfire on "for each land you control" or similar unrelated phrasing.
737:  */

739:   let out = text.replace(/\ball ([a-z][a-z'-]*) creatures\b/gi, (whole, word: string) =>
740:     vocab.typeByWord.has(word.toLowerCase()) ? `${word} creatures you control` : whole,

743:     /\b([a-z][a-z'-]*) you control (get|gain|have|gets|gains)\b/gi,
744:     (whole, word: string, verb: string) =>
745:       vocab.typeByWord.has(word.toLowerCase()) ? `${word} creatures you control ${verb}` : whole,
746:   );

748: }

754:   'Creature',
755:   'Instant',
756:   'Sorcery',
757:   'Artifact',
758:   'Enchantment',
759:   'Land',
760:   'Planeswalker',
761:   'Battle',
762:   'Kindred',

933:   const rawText = row.oracle_text ?? '';
934:   const faceNames = faceNamesIn(row.name);

936:     stripReminderText(stripSelfReferences(rawText, ...faceNames, row.back_name ?? null)),
937:     vocab,
938:   );
939:   const typeLine = row.type_line ?? '';

# CLAUDE.md

Guidance for Claude Code when working in `apps/commander-recommender/`.

## What this is

A Commander recommender: paste or upload a card list, get ranked Commander suggestions —
including Partner/Background pairs — with cited synergies, ban-list legality, and an estimated
Bracket. React 19 + Vite client (Zustand + TanStack Query/Table), Express 5 + better-sqlite3
server, no ORM. Card data is Scryfall's Oracle Cards bulk export, imported into SQLite at
build/deploy time — the running server never calls Scryfall live.

Read [`../../docs/commander-recommender.md`](../../docs/commander-recommender.md) first — it's
this app's own handoff document (moved here during the monorepo consolidation, file map kept
current) and covers the deeper "why" behind the stack choices, the scoring model, and known risk
areas in more depth than this file repeats. This file is about how to work in the code, not what
the code does. The root [`CLAUDE.md`](../../CLAUDE.md) covers workspace-wide commands and
conventions this file doesn't repeat.

## Commands

Run from `apps/commander-recommender/` unless noted (or use `pnpm --filter mtg-recommender-client`
/ `--filter mtg-recommender-server` from the repo root).

- `pnpm --filter mtg-recommender-client dev` and `pnpm --filter mtg-recommender-server dev`, or
  both via `pnpm dev` from the repo root — API on `:4000`, Vite client on `:5173` (proxies `/api`)
- `cd server && pnpm run prepare-data` — downloads Scryfall's Oracle Cards bulk file and seeds
  `server/data/cards.sqlite`; required before `/api/recommend` returns anything but a 503. Needs
  network access; reuses a copy less than a week old unless run as `prepare-data:fresh`
- `cd server && pnpm run typecheck` (`tsc`) / `pnpm run build` (`tsc -p tsconfig.build.json`,
  `src/` only, test files excluded — see the note in `tsconfig.build.json` about why `rootDir`
  matters here) / `pnpm test` (Vitest, 12 files colocated under `src/services/`)
- `cd client && pnpm run typecheck` (`tsc -b`) / `pnpm run build` (`tsc -b && vite build`) /
  `pnpm test` (Vitest, 5 files colocated under `src/lib/`)
- `pnpm run lint` in either — no type-aware rules (see `packages/config/eslint.base.js`)
- Single test file: `pnpm exec vitest run src/services/synergy.test.ts` (or any other), from
  whichever of `client`/`server` it lives in

## Architecture

- **`server/src/services/synergy.ts`** is the heart of the app: builds a `CollectionProfile` from
  the matched cards (color identity, creature types, keywords, oracle-text theme regexes), then
  scores every `CommanderUnit` from `partners.ts` against it. A signal counts only once it clears
  `MIN_SIGNAL_COUNT` (3) distinct supporting cards _after_ narrowing to that unit's color identity.
  Kindred requires the unit's own text to _care_ about a type (`caresAboutCreatureType`), not
  merely have it. Color identity gates eligibility and contributes nothing to score — see the
  "scoring measures focus" tests in `synergy.test.ts` before changing the weight formula.
- **`server/src/services/coverage.ts`** is a second, clearly-labelled tier beneath `synergy.ts`'s
  own two bars, not a lower bar on them — see
  [`../../docs/recommendation-coverage.md`](../../docs/recommendation-coverage.md). Every commander
  already in the submitted list gets suggested regardless of whether it clears `MIN_SIGNAL_COUNT`
  (reason `'owned'`), and a relaxed, narrowest-identity-first pick covers whatever card the
  confident tier still didn't cite (reason `'covers'`). `routes/recommend.ts` sends this as
  `alsoPlayable`, serialized through the same `serialize()`/`cardIndex` the confident `suggestions`
  use — never a second index.
- **`server/src/services/signals.ts`** (879 lines, the largest file) is the signal/role model
  feeding `synergy.ts`: what a card contributes to a deck's plan (`is`/`produces`/`consumes`/
  `rewards`/`amplifies`) and in what capacity. **Read
  [`../../docs/archetypes.md`](../../docs/archetypes.md) before changing this file** — it is the
  reviewable catalog of what those roles and archetypes are _meant_ to mean, derived from twenty real
  decks, and it records which current behaviours are deliberate (so they don't get "fixed") and which
  are known gaps. `deckAnalysis.ts` + `lifecycle.ts` + `packages.ts`
  build on it to answer "what is this list trying to do, and what's it missing" independent of any
  commander — see `docs/commander-recommender.md`'s file map for how those three fit together.
- **`server/src/services/partners.ts`** builds every legal `CommanderUnit` (rule 702.124: one card
  or a legal pair) from the eligible pool — a `CommanderUnit` is what `synergy.ts` scores, not a
  bare `CardRow`. Grouped by ability variant (Partner, Partner—[text], Partner with [Name], Friends
  forever, Choose a Background, Doctor's companion) rather than a cross-product.
- **`server/src/services/eligibility.ts`** judges commander eligibility on a card's **front face
  only** (CR 712.4) — Scryfall's top-level `type_line` for a DFC is both faces joined, which is why
  this can't just substring-match the whole thing. `split` is the deliberate exception (CR 709.4).
  This runs at import time (`import-scryfall.ts`'s only caller), so a stale `cards.sqlite` keeps
  old eligibility until re-imported.
- **`server/src/db.ts`** — SQLite connection + `isSeeded` guard (returns 503 instead of a raw SQL
  error pre-import) + `findCardsByNames`, which falls back to a `card_face_names` table (built by
  `cardNames.ts`'s rules) so a decklist naming only one face of a DFC still resolves.
  `findCardsByOracleIds` is the reverse direction — apps/home's `/profile` page's only way to turn
  a stored `card_preferences` row (oracle_id only) back into a name/image, via `GET /api/cards`
  (`routes/cards.ts`). Both routes' `CardRow` → wire-DTO mapping lives in
  `services/cardDTO.ts` (`toCardDTO`), shared with `routes/recommend.ts` rather than duplicated.
- **`server/scripts/fetch-scryfall.ts`** + **`import-scryfall.ts`** are the only place Scryfall is
  called from this app — see [`../../docs/api-policy.md`](../../docs/api-policy.md), a hard
  project rule, before changing what these call or when. The bulk-snapshot fetch/cache mechanics
  and `User-Agent` are shared with time-counters via `@mtg/scryfall` (`packages/scryfall`); this
  app's own companion fetches (creature types, re-skinned names) and its `IMPORT_VERSION`/sqlite
  `meta`-table freshness check (`dataSnapshot.ts`/`importedSnapshot.ts`) stay local — see
  `docs/handoff.md`'s `@mtg/scryfall` section for why those didn't move.
- **`server/src/services/spellbook.ts`** — Commander Spellbook adapter. Click-triggered only, 1-hour
  in-memory cache, no retry on 429. Same hard-rule constraints apply.
- **Cited-card dedup**: the server sends each cited card once (`server/src/services/cardIndex.ts`)
  and cites it by position; `client/src/lib/rehydrate.ts` puts cards back together at the API
  boundary. This is why a 12MB response became 0.25MB (see `CHANGELOG.md` 1.7.1) — don't bypass it
  by threading whole card objects through a new code path.
- **`client/src/api/`** — `client.ts` (fetch + cold-start retry against Render's free-tier sleep)
  wrapped by `queries.ts` (TanStack Query hooks). The `retry`/`refetchOnWindowFocus`/
  `refetchOnReconnect: false` defaults in `main.tsx` are load-bearing against Commander
  Spellbook traffic — don't restore them without re-reading the api-policy doc.
- **`client/src/store/`** splits by what the state _is_: `useAppStore` (not persisted — textarea
  contents, submitted list, dismissals) vs. `usePreferencesStore` (persisted to `localStorage` —
  durable UI prefs, currently just `combosPerPage`). Don't merge these; a dismissal surviving a
  browser restart against a different pasted list would be surprising, but a durable preference
  should outlive the tab. The suggestion grid itself has no page-size preference any more — it's
  virtualized (`@tanstack/react-virtual`), not paginated, so there's no "how many per page" to
  remember.
- **`client/src/router.tsx`** is the third place client state can live: `RecommendationResults`'
  filters/sort are search params on the one route (`lib/searchSchema.ts`'s
  `validateRecommenderSearch`), not `useState` — shareable and survives a refresh, which neither
  Zustand store's split above was designed for. Its `basepath` reads `import.meta.env.BASE_URL` at
  runtime rather than hardcoding `/` — this app is deployed under `/recommender` as part of the
  combined platform static site (root `CLAUDE.md`'s "Combined deploy"), and `vite.config.ts`'s
  `base` is what actually sets `BASE_URL` per build.
- **`client/src/lib/mtg.ts`** — WUBRG ordering and color-identity naming ("Golgari", never
  "Black/Green"). Mana glyph paths and cost parsing live in `@mtg/mana` (`packages/mana`), shared
  with the sibling app — this client has no `manaSymbols.ts` of its own anymore.
- **Optional sign-in and preferences (Phase 7) live in `@mtg/profile` (`packages/profile`)**, not
  this client's own `store/` — `useAuth`, `useCardPreferences`, `useComboPreferences`, all backed
  by Supabase (RLS, owner-only), plus `AccountMenu`/`AuthDialog` themselves (this client no longer
  has its own copies — it renders `@mtg/ui`'s shared `NavBar` with `@mtg/profile`'s `AccountMenu`
  in its `accountSlot`, same as apps/home and apps/time-counters). `LikeDislikeButtons.tsx`
  (`CommanderCard`'s badge row), `JankToggle` (inside `CardDetailDialog.tsx`), and
  `ComboFavoriteButton.tsx` (inside `ComboFinder.tsx`) are this client's own remaining consumers —
  the annotate-in-place UI apps/home's `/profile` page now also has a browse-and-manage view over.
  `supabase` is `null` when `VITE_SUPABASE_URL`/`VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` aren't set — every
  one of those components checks `useAuth().user` and renders nothing signed out, so the whole
  feature degrades cleanly rather than gating the app on Supabase being configured.
- A suggestion is a `CommanderUnit` (1-2 `CardRow`s), not a single card — every DTO, filter, and
  sort in the client threads through that union, not a flattened card.

## Conventions

- Comments explain _why_, not _what_ — match the existing tone (see `synergy.ts`'s comments on the
  scoring formula, or `eligibility.ts`'s on front-face-only reasoning).
- Keep changes proportional to the ask. This codebase deliberately favors a short, readable
  heuristic over a "complete" system in synergy detection and Bracket estimation — see
  `docs/commander-recommender.md`'s "Core logic" section before making one more sophisticated.
- Match the existing pattern for whichever file you're touching. If the surrounding code uses a
  plain function and a `Set`, don't reach for a class or a new dependency to do the same job.
- **Never write oracle text from memory — copy it from the database.** Scryfall has moved much
  self-referential wording from a card's name to "this creature"/"this land"; two rules in this
  codebase were written from recall and were wrong on real cards (see
  `docs/commander-recommender.md`'s "Known risk areas"). Every string in `signals.test.ts` is
  copied verbatim from the imported database — keep it that way.

  style (see `1.7.1`'s entry for the level of detail expected).
- `docs/commander-recommender.md`'s file map is meant to stay current — update it in the same
  commit whenever you add, rename, or remove a file it lists.
